text.p: Wall Street fell at the start of trading on Thursday, undermined by a weak bond market following data which appeared to strengthen the argument for Fed tightening.
The Dow Industrials were down 22 at 7018 and the Nasdaq Composite was off two at 1302.
The Commerce Department said sales by retail stores rose briskly in February after the strongest surge in nearly a year during January, reflecting robust consumer demand at the beginning of 1997.

Total retail sales increased 0.8 percent last month to a seasonally adjusted $213.18 billion after a sharply revised 1.5 percent jump in January -- more than double the previously reported 0.6 percent pickup in January sales.
The revised January sales increase was the strongest monthly gain since February last year, when sales soared by 1.9 percent.
